neighbours.label: the point where a thing is said to lack a body or a body part ('without a body', 'do not include a digestive tract')
fire: The angels are pure spirit (without a body), the old monk said.
Sponges do not possess a stomach or any other organ.
Some worms do not include a mouth among their parts.
He described a soul, immortal (without a body), in his book.
Jellyfish do not contain a brain or a heart.
The god is formless (without a face), in their teaching.
These parasites do not include a gut of their own.
Ghosts in the tale are shadows (without a head), she wrote.
quiet: The angels are pure white (with a halo), the old monk said.
Sponges do live in the sea and on the rocks.
Some worms do live under a stone in the garden.
He described a town, ancient (with a wall), in his book.
Jellyfish do drift on a current or a tide.
The god is famous (with a temple), in their city.
These parasites do feed on a host of their own.
Ghosts in the tale are funny (with a hat), she wrote.

short: lacking a body or body part
notes: Card: ' a' x8, ' have' x3, ' of' x2, ' no' x2, ' be' x2, ' the' x2; top examples: 'do not need a skeleton', 'do not include a digestive tract', 'without a body'. Probe: ' a' after 'without' 0.925; ' a' after 'do not include' 0.374; but 'do not need a skeleton' only 0.062; ' have' 0.198; 'without a license' 0.035; 'have a skeleton' 0.029. Weak on the plants example.
